rules.basis: Two destination stages with ASYNC_REG for FIFO reset/status/update/ack and MAC TX status; targeted maximum-delay constraints.
Two 14-bit registered Gray read-pointer buses use two-stage synchronization. The remaining two-bit MAC RX status vector carries independent bad-frame and bad-FCS toggle events, not an atomic word.

Two 14-bit committed-write-pointer buses are held stable until a synchronized acknowledgement; the destination samples the bus only after its synchronized update event. Reviewed axis_async_fifo.v lines 388-394, 450-480 and 586-591.

The reported endpoints are external reset to the first PRE pin in each domain's three-stage sync_reset chain. Routed DCP properties independently show all nine cells are FDPE and ASYNC_REG=1. Asynchronous assertion and synchronous local release are intentional.
rules.tool_label_discrepancy: Vivado labels these LUTRAM read/write potential collision, although the endpoints and routed primitive types are reset flip-flops.

no_input_delay_exemptions.reason: External asynchronous reset has no synchronous launch-clock relationship. It asserts local synchronizer preset pins asynchronously and releases through three local-clock stages. Narrow preset/reset-pin exceptions are intentional; no artificial synchronous input delay is assigned.

limitations: Structural/source, routed timing and two clock-ratio simulation evidence; no formal proof or metastability MTBF analysis.
Arbitrary clock ratios, reset sequences and event pulse rates are not exhaustively verified.
Out-of-context clock-source placement is unspecified; 100/125/125 MHz timing is not board clock-distribution or I/O signoff.
